name: Han Wu
bio: Han Wu is dated by Giles to the 8th or 9th century AD. His poem here is a moment of quiet contemplation.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Contemplation
poems.author: Han Wu
poems.text:
When my court-yard by the placid moon is lit,
When around me leaves come dropping from the trees,
On the terrace steps, contemplative, I sit,
The swing-ropes swaying idly in the breeze.

poems.title: Cooler Weather
poems.author: Han Wu
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Her jade-green alcove curtained thick with silk,
Her vermilion screen with its pattern of flowers,
Her eight-foot dragon-beard mat and her quilt brocaded in squares
Are ready now for nights that are neither warm nor cold.
